findings.finding: The business.gov.au paperwork list is accurate, then repeated almost verbatim at the start of the repayment section. Bridging, caveat and second-mortgage distinctions are also restated in the opening, the bullet list, the table and FAQ 3. Article QA paragraph similarity is 0.381. This is repetition, not a new factual claim.

RG 234.40 (June 2026 PDF) says some headline claims are so strong that any separate qualification will not correct any misleading impression. The page keeps the 'some' limiter and the RG 234.34 sentence that the headline claim must not itself be misleading, and it omits the word 'separate'. The link-or-document clause is supported by RG 234.36, which says a link or a document such as a PDS, prospectus or contract will not be sufficient to correct a misleading or deceptive headline claim. The old absolute, that a qualification cannot correct a misleading headline, is gone.

INFO 207 says ASIC encourages anyone who has concerns about commercial lending to seek independent legal advice as soon as possible. The page attributes a narrower form, 'commercial borrowers with concerns', to Information Sheet 207 and does not repeat 'as soon as possible'. The lowest-protection sentence is inside that attribution and matches INFO 207.

sourceClaimMap.claim: A secured business loan uses an asset, such as property, as collateral. If repayments are not made, that asset can be at risk.
The Australian Government's business loan preparation guide says loans vary in costs and conditions, including the term, interest rate, setup costs and ongoing fees.

Business.gov.au identifies proof of identification, a business plan, financial reports (including cash-flow statements if available), financial forecasts, lease agreements, and personal financial information as possible application inputs.
